explanation: Baseline feedback records success on all 10 listed spannerlearning/seed0 tasks under metric_scope "learning"; no failure is observed in that scope, so no defect is demonstrated by the recorded evidence. The revision makes a conservative, behavior-preserving change only: the previous code filtered links with a check that could retain non-location arguments, and it generated pickup candidates by scanning declared spanner types rather than confirmed facts (harmless but wasteful). Links are now filtered by declared type and indexed as a directed adjacency map, and action generation is driven by facts present in the state, mirroring the STRIPS preconditions exactly. A deterministic constructive planner runs first (since tighten_nut consumes spanner usability, each remaining loose nut is assigned a distinct still-usable spanner, with walking to the spanner then to the nut); the previous breadth-first search is retained as a fallback so no previously solved instance is left without an answer. The constructive plan is returned only when the simulated final state satisfies the full goal set; otherwise the search fallback executes, so a returned plan is still grounded and precondition-checked. Nothing here asserts optimality, generalization to unseen instances, or any metric change.
